clue.text: Hot sugary nectar, for starters, in bread — sweet thing

indicators.note: in tells us the hot piece and the starters go inside the bread

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll
hot in the sense of lustful, i.e. randy

indicators.note: for starters asks for the opening letters of sugary and nectar

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a hot, sugary nectar poured over bread makes a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' looks like temperature, but here it means lustful; a bap is a British soft bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a crisp rolled ginger biscuit, a sweet confection.

clue.text: Stay behind cleaner, scrubbing the floor

indicators.note: in a down clue the floor is the bottom letter, and scrubbing removes it from the cleaner

parts.note: a bidet is a bathroom fixture for washing oneself

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay on after the cleaner, scrubbing the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'the floor' is the last letter of BIDET, the T, which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bide is an old verb meaning to remain or wait where one is.

clue.text: Very alert in description of cornfield?

definitions.meaning: a cornfield is wholly made up of ears of corn

explanation.definitionFit: Being fully attentive is an idiom; a field of grain is literally covered in ears.

clue.text: Ground to ascend, soil down

indicators.note: ground as the past of grind, so these words are crushed and reshaped

explanation.surface: Instructions about earthworks: the ground to climb, the soil to be moved downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun but is the past tense of grind, the anagram signal; 'down' is the definition, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being sad, and a disconsolate person is utterly dejected.

clue.text: Bar in heaven, far from stout!

indicators.note: in places the bar within the word for heaven

parts.note: the sky is the heavens above
an inn is a pub, a place with a bar

explanation.surface: A tavern in paradise is no place for a beer belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' suggests the beer to go with the bar, but here it means fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone very thin is the opposite of a portly or heavily built person.

clue.text: Collapse of salt mine bringing complaints

indicators.note: a collapse leaves the words salt and mine in a jumbled heap

explanation.surface: A salt mine caving in brings a wave of grievances from workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaints' looks like grievances, but here it means illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints in the medical sense are minor illnesses or disorders.

clue.text: Rest on instrument, lying back

indicators.note: lying back says the instrument's name is read from its end

parts.note: a tuba is a large brass instrument

explanation.surface: A musician rests on their instrument while lying back.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that border or lean against each other share an edge, as one wall rests on another.

clue.text: Call in Irish opener, as scorer

parts.note: to bell is to call or cry out, and a bell calls people in

indicators.note: the opener of Irish is its first letter

explanation.surface: A phone call in which an Irishman opens the conversation as the team's top scorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests a goalscorer, but here it means one who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini was an Italian opera composer, and composers score music.

clue.text: Fine pass by flipping old twins

parts.note: a ticket is a pass granting entry

indicators.note: flipping turns the little word by over so it reads backwards
twins asks for the abbreviation of old twice

explanation.surface: A permit passed along by mischievous elderly twins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns BY into YB; 'twins' doubles O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickety-boo is old British slang meaning all right or in good order.

clue.text: Expected to entertain several liberals including son (six) not much fun here!

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the word for expected holds the rest within

parts.note: something due is expected or anticipated

indicators.note: including places son and six within the run of liberals

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal, so several of them give a string of L's
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A party of liberals and a six-year-old son is expected for a deadly dull outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'several liberals' gives four L's here, with son and six set in their middle; 'six' in brackets looks like an aside but is Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang place name for anywhere dreary and boring, with a jokey American town suffix.

clue.text: British pass to the west, forming alliance

indicators.note: in an across entry going west means reading right to left

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A British mountain pass to the west forms a political alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties joined for common purposes.

clue.text: In Dutch shoe-cupboard one may die

definitions.text: In Dutch shoe-cupboard one may die

parts.words: In Dutch shoe-cupboard one may die
parts.note: the Dutch wear wooden shoes, and a slang phrase for dying puts them in a cupboard

explanation.definitionFit: A British slang idiom for dying; to pop is to pawn, and clogs are Dutch wooden shoes.

clue.text: Boy on average rejected, then bitterness behind love song

indicators.note: behind places the bitterness after love

parts.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for average reads backwards

parts.note: mean is an average
love is zero in tennis, written as O
bile is bitterness, as in bile against someone

explanation.surface: A boy of average looks is rejected, and his bitterness follows a failed love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the average backwards; 'behind' puts the bitterness after love, which is zero in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous aria from Verdi's opera Rigoletto, sung by the Duke.

clue.text: It's not just food reaching one's empty tummy

indicators.note: reaching places one's next after the food

parts.note: a dish is a prepared item of food
one's taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: empty asks for the tummy with its inside removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: It is unfair that the food only reaches one's empty stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not just' is the definition: unjust conduct, so 'It's' is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying and cheating are behaviour that is unfair and lacking in integrity.

clue.text: Partial to gains, I stake claim

indicators.note: Partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gambler, keen on winnings, places a bet and stakes a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to assert or maintain firmly, as when claiming something is true.

clue.text: Ricotta cooked with last of gravy, a monstrous crime

indicators.note: cooked means the cheese is worked over into a new form
last of asks for the final letter of gravy

explanation.surface: Ricotta cooked in gravy: a culinary outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is a shockingly wicked act, a crime of great cruelty.

clue.text: Air coming in through the window?

definitions.text: Air coming in through the window?

parts.words: Air coming in through the window?
parts.note: air suggests a draught, but here it is a tune sung up to a lover's window

explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is music performed outdoors at night, traditionally beneath a beloved's window.

clue.text: Provider of rooms more sacred outside temple walls

indicators.note: outside places the holier word around the temple's edges

parts.note: holier means more sacred

indicators.note: the walls of temple are its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone renting out rooms beyond the walls of a holy temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walls' asks for the outside letters of temple, which go inside the comparative of sacred.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotelier owns or runs a hotel, a business letting out rooms to guests.

clue.text: In the morning, this device used to flower

parts.note: taken as written
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: In the morning someone uses this gadget to make flowers bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole opening phrase: the device used in the morning is for browning bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen appliance used at breakfast to brown slices of bread.

clue.text: Smoothly, lion bites arm

indicators.note: bites means the lion holds the arm in its jaws

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
a gat is slang for a gun, a firearm

explanation.surface: A lion takes a smooth bite out of someone's arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a limb but is a weapon: GAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning played smoothly, with notes joined together.

clue.text: Criminal finally caught by sailor, in time roaming free

indicators.note: in places the sailor and his catch inside the time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: caught by means the sailor holds the criminal's letter

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of criminal

explanation.surface: A criminal on the loose is finally caught by a sailor just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the criminal's last letter, 'caught by' sets it in the sailor, and 'in' puts that inside the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the loose is not captured and free to wander.

clue.text: Draw, result getting attention

indicators.note: getting places attention after the result

parts.note: an end is an outcome or result
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A drawn match: the result gets everyone's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests a tied game, but here it means attract.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone to you is to make yourself loved by them.

clue.text: Is a fingernail a bit dirty?

definitions.text: Is a fingernail a bit dirty?

parts.words: Is a fingernail a bit dirty?
parts.note: a fingernail sits close to the joint of the finger, and a bit dirty means slightly risqué

explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for humour that is close to being indecent or offensive.

clue.text: Touched cloth

definitions.meaning: a fabric made from pressed matted fibres

explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of feel, and also a dense non-woven fabric made from wool fibres.

clue.text: Son of Adam placed before Messiah, in the end

indicators.note: before places the placed word first

parts.note: set means placed or put down

indicators.note: in the end asks for the last letter of Messiah

explanation.surface: A son of Adam placed before the Messiah at the end of days.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Seth is the third son born to Adam and Eve.

clue.text: People turn the air blue gulping oxygen in Bath, perhaps

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

indicators.note: gulping means the swearing swallows the oxygen

parts.note: to turn the air blue is to swear, i.e. curse
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: People swearing and gasping for air in a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city with a horse-racing course, not a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath, the spa city in Somerset, has a well-known course for horse racing.

clue.text: Space outside where cart tipped over

indicators.note: tipped over means the cart is upended, so read the word backwards

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads such as beer barrels

explanation.surface: A garden space where a cart has overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is an enclosed open area beside a building.

clue.text: Crete's port should be condemned, in hindsight

indicators.note: a condemned building is pulled down, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: Crete's with the possessive s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A Cretan harbour declared unsafe, a judgement reached only looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Crete's' counts here as a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospect is a looking back on past events, the view hindsight gives.
